reference.description: User-provided Promptotyping sphere, mapping source data through a model into research interfaces

prompt: Edit IMAGE 1, the full portrait black-white-purple Pop Art opera singer title illustration. IMAGE 2 is the user's own Promptotyping symbol and is a COMPOSITION reference for the lower portion only. Keep the entire upper opera singer portrait, identity, costume, hair, tiara, pearls, music sheet, hands, magnifying glass, Ben-Day dots, jagged flashes, diagonal divider, purple outer border and overall canvas dimensions unchanged. Change ONLY the lower technical illustration below the diagonal divider. Reinterpret the user's sphere symbol in exactly IMAGE 1's bold black ink, flat white paper, coarse halftone and sparse deep-purple print style. The lower illustration should be one unmistakable transparent SPHERICAL MAPPING SPACE: a large outlined orb seen in perspective, nearly filling the lower panel, with two curved upright internal planes as in IMAGE 2. Preserve the recognizable arc silhouette and cutaway view of the reference sphere rather than merely adding a circle around a flowchart. Left internal curved plane shows archival music source data, a manuscript fragment, music notation and small structured rows; NO DNA or chemistry. In the center, retain the existing opaque BLACK CUBE-HEADED alien with two tiny white dots and sharp irregular tentacles. It represents a black-box model inside the mapping space, and its internals must remain opaque. Tentacles transform/connect the left source plane to the right curved plane, which is a RESEARCH TOOL INTERFACE: a simple facsimile pane beside a structured data table and one tiny chart; no words, no decorative pseudo-code. Visually emphasize mapping source data into a research interface. A small code bracket tile can be held by one tentacle if uncluttered. One restrained purple arrow enters from the source plane, and a purple feedback arc returns from the interface toward the central agent. The singer's existing magnifying glass should remain visually related to the interface below. Keep the lower composition readable at thumbnail size with few large objects and clear white gaps. The sphere is a conceptual container, not a glossy futuristic ball: use thin broken contour arcs and sparse halftone for transparency, NO gradients, blue, orange, glass reflections, glow, 3D render, new human figure, logo, title, captions, or watermark. Exactly one human remains, the original opera singer above. Final output one portrait image, same aspect ratio/dimensions as IMAGE 1.
purpose: Conceptual title illustration. Sphere, curved data and interface planes adapted to the existing opera-singer Pop-Art style.
